Atelectasis: partial loss of lung aeration that produces linear, plate-like, or locally increased pulmonary density
Cardiomegaly: enlargement of the cardiac silhouette relative to the thoracic cavity
Consolidation: airspace filling that obscures normal lung markings and may form a dense focal or multifocal opacity
Edema: pulmonary interstitial or airspace fluid accumulation that may appear diffuse or multifocal
Lung Opacity: a nonspecific increase in pulmonary density that reduces the visibility of underlying lung markings
Pleural Effusion: fluid in the pleural space that changes the normally sharp interface between lung and thoracic boundary
Pneumonia: infectious airspace inflammation that may produce focal, multifocal, or patchy pulmonary opacity
Pneumothorax: air in the pleural space that may produce a visible pleural boundary with reduced peripheral lung markings
